messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Full field-by-field schema for the CALLBACK payload In the materials I have, the online-checkout callback/return examples show typical fields and structures only as samples. There is no full, formal field-by-field reference (all fields + types) for the callback payload documented here. For an authoritative schema, please check with the PayWay Integration Team/product docs owners. 2) Language parameter for the hosted purchase page Yes, the purchase API supports a lang parameter for the hosted checkout:
- Usage (sandbox examples): https://checkout-sandbox.payway.com.kh/api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/purchase?lang={lang} or similarly on UAT/prod purchase URLs.
- Supported locales (per docs): - lang=en → English (default if omitted) - lang=km → Khmer - lang=zh → Chinese
- Notes: - Pass ?lang=<code> on the purchase URL (especially when calling from client-side). - If the page still appears in English, verify the URL really includes ?lang=... and that the redirect retains the parameter. - For some flows (notably some KHQR screens), there are known cases where the lang is ignored and defaults to English; that’s treated as a product-side issue, not an integration mis-use. 3) Customization of hosted checkout (CSS/JS, labels, branding) What’s supported:
- Custom CSS/JS injection is not supported. The hosted checkout JS (checkout2-0.js) and hosted pages are controlled by PayWay; merchants must not modify the hosted JS.
- Branding, logos, payment-method display and some labels are configured per merchant profile on PayWay’s side: - Logos and theme/branding are updated by the PayWay/Integration Team on the merchant profile. Merchant provides the logo asset (typically PNG, correct size), and the team updates it in sandbox and/or production. - Some labels (e.g., success-button label like Continue Shopping → custom text) can be changed either: - Directly by the merchant if the field is exposed in the PayWay merchant portal, or - By the Integration/Support Team on the configuration layer when it’s not merchant-editable. How a merchant requests label/theme changes
1. Decide the exact changes: e.g. - Button label text ("Continue Shopping" → "Continue Booking"). - Any wording on the hosted success screen. - Updated logo assets or “We Accept” logos.
2. Request through the Integration/PayWay team (or via your merchant portal if the relevant fields are exposed): - Provide: merchant ID, environment (sandbox/production), and the exact label text/assets to apply. - If using the portal, update the editable text fields and logo assets under profile/settings where available.
3. The Integration Team updates the profile/config, then you retest the hosted checkout to confirm labels/branding and redirects (e.g. continue_success_url) behave as expected. So in summary: language is controlled via ?lang=..., UI theming/labels/branding are centrally configured by PayWay (plus limited portal-side fields), and direct CSS/JS customization of the hosted page is not supported.

messages.text:
Part 1/2 Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Can completion be <, =, or > original hold?
From the current docs:
- General pre-auth rule: completion must not exceed the original pre-auth amount.
- For supported card pre-authorisation transactions, PayWay can allow capture above the original hold within a tolerance of about 10% (config- and scheme-dependent). So for card pre-auth specifically:
- Lower than hold → supported (partial capture).
- Equal to hold → supported.
- Slightly higher → allowed up to ~10% over the original amount for supported card pre-auth, not for large increases. 2) When is the uncaptured remainder released?
Two cases described:
- When you complete (capture) with a lower amount, the remaining pre-authorised amount is automatically released back to the customer by the gateway after the completion is processed.
- If you never complete or cancel within the pre-auth validity window (e.g. up to ~30 days), the entire hold auto-reverses/auto-cancels and funds are released according to issuer/card-network rules. 3) Capture vs cancel race condition
The pre-auth lifecycle docs describe:
- Separate complete-preauth (capture) and cancel-preauth operations, and
- Retry/error handling and offline/manual fallbacks, but they do not define behaviour for a true race where capture and cancel are submitted at the same time against the same pre-auth. The expected outcome of that race is not specified in this KB; integrators are expected to avoid it (decide one action in your own system and ensure only that request is sent). 4) Incremental auth / re-auth support
Documented behaviour:
- PayWay does not currently expose a merchant API for incremental authorisation against an existing pre-auth (no multiple "+X" increments on the same hold).
- PayWay does not expose a dedicated merchant-facing Re-Authorisation API for continuously renewing an existing pre-auth.
- Instead, for small changes you can rely on the ~10% over-capture tolerance, and for longer/more variable scenarios the guidance is to design around Card-on-File/Credential-on-File tokenisation + new authorisations. 5) Detecting auto-release at end of the capture window
Docs say:
- Pre-auth has a validity/hold period (commonly up to 30 days; may be configured per merchant/platform).
- If not completed/cancelled within that window, the hold auto-reverses.
- There is no webhook/callback for automatic cancel or complete of pre-auth; integrations should rely on API responses and portal status checks. So yes: to detect auto-release, the intended approach is to use /api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/check-transaction-2 (and/or the merchant portal) to poll/check the pre-auth status rather than expecting a callback. 6) Issuer/central-bank constraints, refund timing, and recovering the original pre-auth for refund
From the lifecycle/operational notes:
- If online completion/cancellation or related refund operations fail due to issuer or gateway issues, you should: - Retry the online operation where appropriate, and - If still not possible, follow the offline/manual refund/cancel process via bank forms and settlement team. Those offline reversals can take time and may not immediately reflect in the portal; timing depends on issuer/card-network/operations and is not quantified in this KB.
- For reconciliation and later refunds, you are expected to: - Store and track identifiers such as tran_id (and any pre-auth reference IDs), and - Use Check Transaction API and/or the merchant portal to locate the transaction using tran_id / APV / order IDs and status. - For offline/manual correction, the docs say to reconcile using APV/order IDs and evidence (receipts, approvals) with the settlement/integration team, who can then update the status where required.

messages.text:
Part 1/2 Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Based on the payout/split materials in the docs: 1) Source account / currency for payout Docs describe payout/split as distributing funds from the merchant’s settlement/platform sub‑account to whitelisted beneficiary accounts/MIDs. They also note that if the beneficiary account currency doesn’t match the payment/merchant currency, you can get errors like PTL147 "Payment currency is not allowed." There’s no statement that any account other than the configured settlement/platform account(s) can be used as the source, nor any support for cross‑currency funding – so the safe assumption from docs is: payout comes from the merchant’s own settlement/sub‑account in the same currency. 2) Fees, limits, rounding, fee allocation The payout docs here do not specify: - Per‑transaction/daily limits, - Fee structure for payout/split, or - How any fees are allocated across beneficiaries. They only state that the merchant must define explicit payout amounts and ensure the sum matches their intended distribution, and that standard currency formatting rules apply. All details on fees, limits and allocation need to come from PayWay commercial/ops configuration, not from this KB snapshot. 3) Where to see source debit and beneficiary credits The Payout overview states you can: - "Easily manage and track customer & payout transactions through the PayWay Merchant Portal or ABA Merchant app." So, from docs: portal + ABA Merchant app are the official places to see payout flows (source vs beneficiaries). It doesn’t go into which exact report names/columns show the split. 4) add‑whitelist‑payout payee format & sandbox accounts What’s documented:
- Beneficiaries can be: - MIDs (for card split/payout – card split supports beneficiary as MID only), or - Whitelisted ABA accounts (for payout in general). - For production, "All destination/payout accounts used in production must be whitelisted" and must be real ABA accounts (via bank process or whitelist API). - For sandbox, you must not use real bank accounts: - "Do not use real bank accounts in sandbox; use the sandbox whitelist accounts provided by Integration Team for testing." The docs do not spell out the exact payee field format (pure account number vs customer ID) – only that they are ABA accounts or MIDs and must be whitelisted. The generic PTL04 on invalid accounts matches the “parameter validation” rule, but there’s no finer‑grained error doc here. 5) complete‑with‑payout on sandbox profile ec476910 (PTL62) For pre‑auth completion with payout the rules are:
- Split/Payout is an additional service; it must be explicitly enabled for the merchant by the Integration Team. - Beneficiaries must be pre‑whitelisted and the merchant must be provisioned for that service. The KB does not define PTL62, but it does say that sending payout parameters when the service is not enabled or merchant profile not configured will result in merchant‑configuration errors. So this error is consistent with: your merchant profile is not provisioned for complete‑with‑payout in sandbox. Whether ec476910 can be provisioned is not something the docs can answer; that’s up to the Integration/ops team to enable on that profile. 6) List of seeded sandbox beneficiary accounts Docs are explicit that sandbox test beneficiary accounts are provided by the Integration Team for payout testing and that real bank accounts must not be used in sandbox, but there is no embedded list of those test accounts in this KB. You’ll need the team to share the seeded sandbox beneficiary details separately.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Based on what’s documented about refunds (policy, not mechanics): 1) Refund window after capture
Refunds via portal or Refund API are documented as available:
- Within a configurable online refund window, described consistently as about 30 days from the original transaction date.
- After that window, online/API refund is not available and you must use the manual/offline refund process via PayWay/merchant support (cancellation/refund form, signed by an authorized person). 2) Multiple partial refunds up to the original total
The docs state that full and partial refunds are supported (via portal and API) within the refund window, but they do not explicitly say whether multiple partial refunds against the same transaction are allowed up to the original amount. That behaviour (how many partials, remaining‑amount rules) isn’t specified here and would need confirmation from the Integration/Operations team. 3) Refund fees and who is authorized to trigger refunds
What’s documented:
- Fees: - For ABA‑to‑ABA refunds (same‑bank account payments), docs note no refund processing fee. - For some KHQR offline/manual refunds, docs say there is no fee and processing can take several working days. - For other methods, and in production generally, fees are not fully specified; guidance is to confirm with the commercial/merchant agreement or PayWay support.
- Who can trigger refunds: - Portal refunds: any user with the appropriate merchant portal permissions can initiate full/partial refunds within the allowed window. - API refunds: your backend can issue refunds using the Refund API with the merchant’s credentials/keys. - Offline/manual refunds: require a bank form signed by an authorized signatory for the merchant account (following specimen/signature rules) and processed by bank/merchant support. 4) Rounding/minimums for partial refunds
In this refund‑policy set, the docs:
- Confirm that partial refunds are supported.
- Do not restate the exact currency scale rules for refund amounts (e.g., 0.01 USD vs whole KHR) or any minimum refund amount beyond general statements like “a portion of the transaction”.
So from this material alone, I can’t definitively confirm:
- Whether partial refund amounts always follow the original currency’s scale (e.g. 0.01 USD / 1 KHR),
- Or any concrete minimum per refund (for either currency).
Those details would need to be taken from the core amount/format specs or checked with the Integration team. 5) Refunds after payout/split
The refund docs here cover standard gateway transactions (card, ABA PAY, KHQR, etc.), via portal/API and offline, but they do not mention payout/split flows at all. So I can’t confirm from this KB whether manual refund is the only path after a payout/split – that behaviour would need to be clarified with the PayWay product/ops team.

messages.text:
[Part 1/2] Hello Bong @Ruzaid, **1) Amount rules (USD/KHR, min/max, sub‑100‑KHR refunds)**
- Docs are clear on **format** for all payment operations (Purchase, QR, Refund and other payment requests): - **USD:** decimal string with **exactly 2 decimal places**. - Examples: `"0.01"`, `"0.10"`, `"1.46"`, `"2500.00"` - **KHR:** **integer only**, no decimal point at all. - Examples: `"16000"`, `"11300"`
- Do **not** include currency symbols or text inside `amount` (no `$`, `៛`, `USD`, `KHR`, commas, spaces). Currency goes in the `currency` field.
- These formatting rules apply consistently across the payment APIs mentioned (Purchase / QR / Refund); the docs treat them as **global amount rules**.
- **Per‑method minimum/maximum:** - Explicitly documented only for **USD refunds**: must be formatted with 2 decimals and be **at least `0.01`** and **not exceed the remaining refundable amount**. - Any other concrete min/max values (including for KHR, payouts, or overall transaction ceilings) are **not specified** here; they are described as limits defined by the commercial agreement / gateway configuration. If you hit `Invalid Transaction Amount`, you’re expected to validate formatting and then check configured limits.
- **Sub‑100‑KHR refunds:** there is **no explicit statement** on accepting values below 100 KHR (e.g. `"50"`) in the docs provided, so I can’t confirm whether those are allowed or rejected in production. **2) tran_id and merchant identifiers (chars, length, uniqueness)**
- For `tran_id` the documented rules are: - Max length: **20 characters**. You should enforce `length <= 20` before sending. - Allowed characters: **alphanumeric**; a **hyphen (`-`) is allowed in some integrations**. Other special characters and spaces are discouraged. - Examples of safe IDs: `"INV202510021234"`, `"ORDER-12345"` (<= 20 chars).
- **Uniqueness / scope:** - The rules state that **duplicate `tran_id` will be rejected** (duplicate transaction ID error), but they **do not explicitly say** whether that uniqueness is global or scoped per merchant profile. - So all we can rely on from docs is: **treat `tran_id` as unique for your usage; reusing the same value for a different transaction can trigger a duplicate error**, except for the special case where QR retries reuse the same `tran_id` for the *same* payment flow.
- For **other merchant references** (e.g. `return_param` / `return_params`): - Current materials do **not define strict character/length constraints**; they only state that `return_param(s)` must **not be included in the hash**. There’s no canonical max length/charset documented here. **3) Timezone for timestamps, and units for lifetime/expiry**
- **Timestamps:** - `req_time` and similar fields must follow the expected **14‑digit timestamp format** (e.g. `"20260212144826"` — `YYYYMMDDhhmmss`). - The **timezone** for these gateway timestamps is **not specified** in the docs available here, so I can’t definitively state UTC vs local; you should treat them as opaque server timestamps and confirm the timezone with the Integration team if you need precise alignment.
- **lifetime / expiry units:** - The docs acknowledge that payment sessions have an expiry window (e.g. QR sessions commonly expiring around **15 minutes**) and recommend polling `check-transaction` for up to about **5 minutes** after QR creation. - There is a `lifetime` field shown in examples (e.g. `"lifetime": 3`) but the **unit (seconds vs minutes)** is **not explicitly defined** in the retrieved material. - Likewise, generic expiry fields (QR lifetime / payment link `expired_date`) are required to be **valid and in the future**, but their **unit/zone are not formally specified** here beyond using the documented timestamp/datetime formats.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, 1) Effect of payment_gate=0 and profile‑specific routing Yes. When a merchant profile has both Ecommerce Checkout and QR/API services enabled, payment_gate determines which behavior /api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/purchase returns:
- payment_gate=0 → E‑commerce Checkout flow (hosted checkout / webpage response, i.e. HTML/redirect style),
- payment_gate omitted or set for QR/API → QR/API response (QR fields like qr_string, qr_img). So the effect is profile‑specific: it matters when both services are enabled on that merchant profile. 2) Is payment_gate still supported on /purchase? Yes. The current rules explicitly describe payment_gate on:
https://checkout.payway.com.kh/api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/purchase
including how it switches between hosted checkout and QR JSON when both services are enabled. It is still a supported parameter there and should be set explicitly when both QR API and Ecommerce Checkout are active. 3) view_type=hosted_view — mobile‑only or also desktop? Docs distinguish by channel:
- Desktop web (popup checkout): use the JS plugin + iframe target; view_type is not required.
- Mobile browser / H5 / in‑app WebView: pass view_type=hosted_view to get a full‑screen hosted checkout URL that you load in a WebView. So hosted_view is documented as the mechanism for mobile/H5/app & WebView flows. Desktop popup flows are expected to use the JS plugin without view_type. The docs don’t prohibit it on desktop, but they only specify it for mobile/H5/WebView, and say desktop popup shouldn’t rely on it.

Hello Bong @Ruzaid,
**1) Cancel / pause / resum…
messages.text:
[Part 1/2] Hello Bong @Ruzaid, **1) Cancel / pause / resume subscription**
From the docs we have for scheduled payments:
- Subscription is **initiated** via the `subscription` flow (`token_flag=CITR_FIX`, `frequency=1W/1M/2M`).
- Subsequent charges are **merchant‑initiated** via the normal **Payment API** using the stored token (`MITR_FIX`).
- Merchants must provide UI to **“Unsubscribe – allow customers to cancel an existing subscription so no future payments will be charged.”**
- Tokens themselves have a lifecycle: `status` (0=removed, 1=active, 2=frozen) and `expired_at`. Users can **freeze/unfreeze/remove/renew** tokens from ABA Mobile, and these changes can be pushed back to the merchant via CoF callbacks. However, in this KB snapshot there is **no dedicated "cancel/pause/resume subscription" API documented** beyond general token lifecycle/CoF management. It only describes:
- Stopping your **own scheduled MITR job** for that `ctid`/token, and/or
- Relying on token status changes (removed/frozen/expired) to prevent further MITR charges. Any specific `remove-token` / freeze / pause endpoints beyond the `renew-expired-account-token` endpoint are not detailed here. ---
**2) How merchant learns about each renewal charge**
For scheduled payments, the flow is:
- Your batch job calls **Payment API** (MITR_FIX) for each due subscription.
- For **every processed payment**, PayWay sends a **payment completion callback (webhook)** to your `callback_url`.
- The documented sample pushback for scheduled payments is:
```json
{ "tran_id": "17425401324", "apv": "619195", "status": "0", "return_params": "xxxxxxxxxx"
}
```
This is the **same structure as a normal Payment API pushback**; docs do **not** define a different schema for “recurring vs one‑off” — the difference is your own context (`ctid`, `token_flag`, subscription record) and which batch call originated it. So: **yes, there is a callback per recurring charge**, and it follows the standard payment pushback format. ---
**3) Frequency vs token expiry / 90‑day rule**
The explicit 90‑day rolling expiry is only documented for **unscheduled account tokens with flags `CITI_FLEX` and `CITO_FLEX`** via the Renew Token API:
- *“Account tokens linked with the `CITI_FLEX` or `CITO_FLEX` flags will expire 90 days after their initial linking, renewal, or the last successful transaction—whichever is most recent.”* For **CITR_FIX / MITR_FIX** (scheduled subscriptions):
- Token callbacks for subscriptions include `expired_at`, `status`, `token_flag=CITR_FIX`, `frequency`, and `subscribed_amount`.
- FAQs state: *“No, expired tokens cannot be used to process payments… If a frozen or expired token is used, the transaction will be declined.”* But the docs **do not state any 90‑day rule for CITR_FIX/MITR_FIX**, nor do they say that `frequency` has any control over token expiry. They are treated as **separate concepts**:
- `frequency` = billing schedule (1W/1M/2M) for your MITR job.
- `expired_at` / token status = independent token lifecycle; if the token is expired or frozen, the scheduled MITR charge will fail. So from the docs: a **CITR_FIX token can expire**, and if it does, further charges will be declined. The exact expiry policy (whether it mirrors the 90‑day rule or something else) is **not specified** here for CITR_FIX. ---
**4) Simulating a full recurring cycle in sandbox**
In the retrieved material there is **no described shortcut to accelerate 1W/1M/2M cycles** for scheduled payments in sandbox. The sandbox notes only mention that:
- Sandbox **may** support some special test flows (e.g. token expiry manipulation) for CoF in general, and
- Standard guidance is to run your own scheduled jobs and use sandbox Payment + callbacks/Check‑Transaction for verification.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Here’s what is covered in the current documentation for Payment Link voiding, and where it’s silent: 1) Production availability, path/signing, docs page
Docs state that a payment link can be voided both via the PayWay Merchant Portal and via the API, and that:
- Voiding deactivates the link so it cannot accept further payments.
- Voiding is irreversible. However, the materials here do not specify:
- The exact production endpoint path (only that an API exists),
- The signing/encryption scheme for that endpoint, or
- Whether a dedicated public doc page is planned for /payment-link/void. Those details need to be confirmed with the Integration Team / product owners. 2) Can PAID / partially‑paid multi‑payment links be voided, and what code?
The docs only say:
- Merchants can void a payment link to prevent further payments.
- Once voided, the link is permanently deactivated and cannot be reactivated. They do not state whether:
- A fully PAID link or a partially‑paid multi‑use link can be voided, or
- Which error code is returned if such a void is rejected. So this behavior (and any PTL mapping) is not defined in the KB I have. 3) In‑flight payments when a link is voided
Documented behavior for voiding is focused on future access:
- After void, customers who open the link see that it is no longer valid, and it can no longer accept payments. The docs do not describe:
- What happens to already in‑flight payments initiated before the void,
- Whether their pushbacks still fire, or
- Whether check‑transaction still returns APPROVED for those payments if they later succeed. So the exact interaction between void timing and in‑flight transactions is not specified here. 4) PTL188 for double void
The PTL error section in this KB only documents some codes (e.g., PTL06, PTL62, PTL175, etc.). Codes like PTL188 are not defined in the available material, so I don’t have an official mapping for “double void” or confirmation that PTL188 is the final production code for that scenario. 5) Refund vs void for paid links
Docs differentiate the two operations conceptually:
- Refund (via portal/API) returns money to the customer according to the refund rules; used to correct/return a payment.
- Void payment link (via portal/API) permanently deactivates the link so no further payments can be made, and once voided it cannot be reactivated; if a similar link is needed, merchants should duplicate or create a new link. However, the KB does not prescribe a strict rule like “merchants should always refund instead of voiding paid links” or specify any mandatory sequence between refunding and voiding. It only states behavior and irreversibility; policy on how to combine them for PAID links is left to merchant/business rules and PayWay product guidance. For all the points above that touch endpoint path, signing, PTL188/PTL132 mappings, or PAID/partially‑paid void semantics, you’ll need confirmation from the PayWay Integration/Ops team as they’re not spelled out in the current documentation snapshot.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Here’s what’s documented vs what isn’t for Payment Link: 1) Server‑side EXPIRED status vs local enforcement
- Docs state that when expired_date is set, PayWay honors expiration and “if an expiry date is set on the Payment Link, requests after expiry must be rejected; conversely, an unlimited payment configuration should remain active until revoked.”
- That implies expiry is enforced on the PayWay side, not purely by the merchant.
- However, a specific link‑level "EXPIRED" status field/contract isn’t described. The contract is: set a valid future expired_date, and after that time the link should not be usable; merchants may still implement local guards but shouldn’t have to be the only enforcement. 2) Canonical production types (create/detail/pushback)
From the documented rules:
- Request fields - amount (Payment Link create) must be sent as a string (e.g. "100.00"). - payment_limit must also be a string. - expired_date must be a string datetime in the expected format and represent a future time.
- Response / pushback fields (generic gateway rules) - tran_id: treated as an identifier; docs do not fix it to numeric vs string, and also warn that link‑level tranid and transaction‑level tranid differ. Safest contract is to treat tran_id as a string in your integration model and accept either numeric or string JSON from the gateway. - amount, totalAmount in pushbacks/check‑transaction: documented as numeric. - status: may be numeric or enum, with 0 used as the success example. - datetime and payment_type: optional.
- total_refund and expired_date in responses - There is no explicit type contract for total_refund in the docs provided. - For expired_date in responses, only the format/"future time" requirement is documented; special sentinel values like string "0" are not specified as part of the contract. So: your implementation should treat IDs and datetimes as strings, monetary values as decimals/numerics, and be tolerant of numeric vs string for IDs in JSON, rather than relying on sandbox’s exact shapes. 3) When is pushback_url present in detail responses?
- The Payment Link detail response schema and pushback_url field behavior are not described in the available documentation. There is no rule stating when it must appear or be omitted. 4) Minimum future expired_date offset & error codes for invalid values
- Documented rules: - expired_date must be in the exact expected format and must represent a future time. - “Incorrect expired_date causes failures.”
- There is no documented minimum offset (e.g. +1 minute vs +1 hour), and no specific PTL code is tied to “past” or “too‑soon” expired_date in the material here. 5) PTL04, PTL05, PTL99, PTL132 mappings
- The PTL section explicitly documents only some codes (e.g. PTL06 – request expired, PTL62 – invalid merchant info, PTL175 – origin not whitelisted, etc.).
- PTL04, PTL05, PTL99, PTL132 are not defined in the provided documentation, nor are their condition mappings for Payment Link. So, from this context:
- You can rely on server‑side enforcement of link expiry via expired_date, correct typing for request fields (amount/payment_limit as strings, future expired_date string), and numeric amount/totalAmount with numeric/enum status in pushbacks.
- But the exact link EXPIRED status field, pushback_url presence rules, minimum expiry offset, and PTL04/05/99/132 definitions are not specified and would need confirmation from the PayWay Integration/Ops team.

- `0` represents success in the pushback examples.
- Other concrete numeric values and meanings are **not documented** here; you’ll need Integration/Ops to confirm the full set for Payment Link. 3) **Multiple pushbacks per payment** Yes. The generic pushback rule explicitly states:
- Gateway **may send multiple pushback events for the same `tranid** (e.g. when status changes).
- Integrators must design **idempotent** handling (update if status changed, ignore no‑ops). So for Payment Links as well, you should **assume more than one pushback per payment is possible** and build idempotent processing on tranid`. 4) **Error for invalid/unknown link id (PTL132 vs 96)** The available pushback/returnurl and inquiry docs in this context do not define PTL132 or the sandbox’s HTTP 403 code 96 "Invalid merchant data" for Payment Links, nor do they state which of these is the canonical production response. messages.text:
[Part 1/2] Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Answering based on what’s documented about inquiry/reconciliation and offline KHQR flows: **1) Proof of payment vs check-transaction / transaction-detail**
- The recommended **primary proof** is still the **callback (pushback/webhook)** – you should log and verify that payload and use it to update your ledger.
- For **reconciliation / recovery** when callbacks are missing or in doubt, docs recommend: - Use **Check Transaction** when you already know `transaction_id` for **recent status verification**. - Use **`get-transactions-by-mc-ref`** or **`transaction-detail`** for richer historical info (including amounts/currency, refund_amount, etc.).
- Check Transaction is explicitly described only as a status check (7‑day window; see Q4); the richer fields (including original/payment amount & currency) are documented on: - `get-transactions-by-mc-ref` (returns `original_amount`, `original_currency`, `payment_amount`, `payment_currency`, etc.), and - `transaction-detail` (same types of fields plus operations/history). There is **no documented pattern** that guarantees *“full financial proof including original_currency only from callback + check-transaction”* without ever calling one of the richer inquiry APIs. If you need a complete, independently re‑queryable proof set, the docs implicitly assume **paced use of `get-transactions-by-mc-ref` and/or `transaction-detail`** on top of callback + Check Transaction. ---
**2) Recovering from lost create/refund/capture/payout responses**
From the reconciliation/missed-callback guidance:
- For a **lost create‑payment (QR) response** where you still know the `tran_id` you used: - Use **Check Transaction** on that `transaction_id` to get the final status.
- For **missing callbacks / lost create responses when you rely on merchant_ref**: - Use **`get-transactions-by-mc-ref`** with your `merchant_ref` to search for matching APPROVED transactions and reconcile them back to the invoice/bill.
- For **refund visibility and other operations (capture/payout)**: - The **`transaction-detail`** API is documented as returning `refund_amount`, operations/history, etc., and is the canonical way to reconstruct the full lifecycle when you already know the PayWay `transaction_id`. So the documented, reliable recovery keys are:
- **`transaction_id` → Check Transaction / transaction-detail** (recent vs historical details), and
- **`merchant_ref` → get-transactions-by-mc-ref** (invoice‑centric recovery and investigation). No separate “lost‑refund‑response” recovery endpoint is described; the flow is always: **identify the transaction, then query by `transaction_id` or `merchant_ref` with the above APIs**. ---
**3) Can a QR / payment link be paid more than once? Duplicate identity rules**
Yes – the docs explicitly cover the case where the **same QR is genuinely paid twice**:
- The **second payment gets a different PayWay `transaction_id`**.
- It is treated as a **new payment**, not a duplicate webhook.
- Your system must **store it and classify it** according to the invoice balance (UNPAID / PARTIALLY_PAID / PAID / OVERPAID / EXCEPTION, etc.). Identity / deduplication rules from the offline KHQR guidance:
- **Deduplication key:** - Use **`transaction_id`** to detect duplicate callbacks and avoid double‑booking the same payment.
- **Reconciliation key:** - Use **`merchant_ref`** to map a transaction to the correct invoice or account.
- **Important:** - *“Do not deduplicate merely because another payment already exists for the same `merchant_ref`, because multiple legitimate transactions may share the same reference.”* These rules apply generically to PayWay payment records (QR, links, etc.):
- Same QR/link can yield **multiple APPROVED payments**.
- Each APPROVED operation has its own **`transaction_id`** and should be booked, then classified (e.g. overpayment or multiple installments) by your invoice logic.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, I'll go by question. 1) Sandbox only showing paid / checkout-created txns – is that the intended contract?
The documented contract for transaction-list is:
- It is a reconciliation/listing API that returns transactions filtered by date, amount, status, outlet, etc.
- It’s positioned for reconciliation and historical lookup, not as a real‑time pending‑status feed; for that, docs say to use Check Transaction while the QR is active. The docs do not explicitly state that all unpaid/open QR transactions must appear in transaction-list, nor that all internal check-transaction‑visible records are guaranteed to surface there. So the behavior you see in sandbox (only paid/checkout‑created txns listed; unpaid open QR‑only not listed) is not contradicted by the spec, and there is no published guarantee that open/unpaid QRs are included in the list in production. 2) Any filter/variant that includes unpaid open QR transactions?
From the documented inquiry patterns:
- transaction-list – list for reconciliation with date/status filters (no mode documented that “also shows unpaid/open QR sessions”).
- get-transactions-by-mc-ref – returns up to 50 matching transactions for a given merchant_ref, used for invoice investigation, callback recovery, duplicate‑payment checks, etc.
- check-transaction – for recent payment‑status verification when you already know transaction_id. There is no documented filter or variant of transaction-list (or get-transactions-by-mc-ref) that is specified to include still‑open, unpaid QR transactions as a way to track abandoned‑but‑scannable QRs. The recommended contract in docs is:
- Track open QRs on your side when you create them.
- Use Check Transaction for their live status while active.
- Use transaction-list / transaction-detail / get-transactions-by-mc-ref for paid/historical reconciliation, not to enumerate open sessions. 3) 3‑day date window cap – same in production, and can it be raised per merchant?
Docs state for transaction-list / transaction-list-2:
- Max date range per request is 3 days (inclusive of today).
- Applies across environments; larger ranges can trigger errors (403/500 or similar).
- Guidance is to use pagination and multiple 3‑day windows or portal exports for larger ranges. There is also a sandbox‑specific note for transaction-list-2 about a 3‑day window within a 30‑day period, but the 3‑day per‑request cap itself is documented as a general rule (not sandbox‑only). The docs do not mention any per‑merchant override of this cap. They instead recommend:
- Keeping API ranges ≤ 3 days.
- Using other reporting/export mechanisms or future/new endpoints if very large exports are needed. So from the published contract: yes, assume the 3‑day cap applies in production as well, and treat it as fixed unless PayWay explicitly provisions a different reporting mechanism for you.

Hello Bong @Ruzaid, From the documented rules on limits and rate‑control, I can only partially answer your questions — the exact per‑endpoint numbers you list are not published. 1) Confirm/correct limits for PRODUCTION
- The only explicit numeric production limit documented is for KHQR generation: - “Default limit for KHQR generation is 10 calls per second per Merchant ID.”
- For Check Transaction the docs only give examples and best practices, not a hard limit: - Avoid tight per‑second polling. - Example guidance seen: 20 requests/second initially; PayWay can consider 50 requests/second on negotiation (and must be confirmed with operations).
- For transaction‑detail, transaction‑list, refund, get‑transactions‑by‑mc‑ref, there are no published numeric limits in the spec. So your sandbox‑observed values (e.g., 600/min, 10/min, 50/min, 500/s, 10/min) cannot be confirmed or corrected from the documentation I see; they need explicit confirmation from PayWay Ops/Engineering for production. 2) HTTP 429 with Retry‑After header
- The spec states that HTTP 429 Too Many Requests indicates rate limiting and that clients should back off.
- It does not state that a Retry-After header is present today, nor does it describe a roadmap/plan for adding it. 3) Penalty model (what is limited, and for how long)
Documented behavior is mixed, by feature:
- Per‑merchant limits: - KHQR generation is explicitly rate‑limited per Merchant ID (10 req/s per MID).
- IP‑based protections / blocking: - For Check Transaction and general API usage, docs say the gateway may rate‑limit or block IPs that send too many requests in a short time and recommend coordinating with support if that happens. - The sandbox merchant portal specifically can block IPs with “Access denied Error code 1020” when it detects abnormal automated access. The precise penalty model (exact thresholds, whether each API is enforced per key vs per merchant vs per IP, and how long a block lasts) is not specified in the documentation; the guidance is only to slow polling, implement backoff, and contact support if you hit 429s/blocks. 4) Production 429 response body
- The docs only refer to HTTP status 429 Too Many Requests as the rate‑limit signal.
- They do not define a canonical JSON body schema or numeric error code for 429 in production (e.g., whether there is a code field like 429 in the body). So in summary: only KHQR’s 10 req/s per MID and example 20–50 rps guidance for Check Transaction are explicitly documented; the rest of the detailed limits and the exact 429 payload/penalty behavior need confirmation from the Integration/Ops team.

messages.text:
Hello Bong @Ruzaid, Based on the current specs, the production‑valid token_flag values are: ### 1) Account / card linking
Endpoints: Link Account, Link Card Valid token_flag values:
- CITI_FLEX – CIT Initial / variable amount, customer‑initiated, unscheduled
- CITO_FLEX – CIT Other / variable amount, merchant‑initiated later (MIT), unscheduled These are the only token flags documented for linking. They create unscheduled CoF tokens. ➡️ CITR_FIX is not a valid value on linking endpoints; by design, linking uses CITI_FLEX / CITO_FLEX only. --- ### 2) Charging with a token (Payment API)
Endpoint: Payment (purchase with token) From the unscheduled and scheduled token docs:
- CITU_FLEX – CIT Unscheduled, variable amount (customer uses a previously saved method)
- MITU_FLEX – MIT Unscheduled, variable amount (merchant charges on demand, no fixed schedule)
- MITR_FIX – MIT Recurring, fixed amount (subsequent scheduled/subscription charges using the stored token) So for token‑based charges in production, the documented flags are:
- CITU_FLEX
- MITU_FLEX
- MITR_FIX (You will see CITR_FIX in the token metadata for subscription tokens, but the charge itself is done with MITR_FIX.) --- ### 3) Subscription registration
Endpoint: Subscription (CITR registration step) Valid token_flag value:
- CITR_FIX – CIT Recurring, fixed amount (customer‑initiated registration with fixed schedule/amount; e.g. 1W/1M/2M) The token callback for scheduled payments also documents:
- token_flag: possible values = CITR_FIX
- frequency: 1W, 1M, 2M So subscription registration uses only:
- CITR_FIX (with frequency 1W/1M/2M) --- ### About undocumented values (e.g. CITO_FIX, CITR_FLEX)
In the docs I have, the only allowed values are:
- Unscheduled: - CITI_FLEX, CITO_FLEX (linking) - CITU_FLEX, MITU_FLEX (charging)
- Scheduled: - CITR_FIX (subscription registration) - MITR_FIX (subsequent scheduled charges) Values like CITO_FIX or CITR_FLEX do not appear anywhere in the published specification as valid flags. Given that:
- They should be treated as unsupported / out of contract, even if sandbox currently accepts them on some calls.
- For production‑grade clients, the recommendation is to only generate and accept the documented token_flag set above, and to reject or ignore any other variants. So, to your last point explicitly: yes, per spec CITR_FIX is intentionally invalid on the linking endpoints; linking is restricted to CITI_FLEX / CITO_FLEX, subscription registration uses CITR_FIX, and subsequent subscription charges use MITR_FIX.

> "Account tokens linked with the `CITI_FLEX` or `CITO_FLEX` flags will expire 90 days after their initial linking, renewal, or the last successful transaction—whichever is most recent."
So every renewal or successful transaction pushes the expiry out another ~90 days. 2) Timezone for the boundary The docs explicitly specify UTC for request timestamps like request_time (e.g. in renew-expired-account-token), but they do not state the timezone used to compute the 90‑day token validity / boundary. There’s no authoritative statement tying token-expiry calculation to a specific timezone in what I have, so for this point you’ll need confirmation from the Integration Team. 3) Error code when charging an EXPIRED (not removed) token The FAQs state that:
- Expired tokens cannot be used, and
- The user sees an ABA Mobile notification that the payment method is no longer valid. However, there is no documented gateway error code (status/code) for "token expired but not removed" in the materials available here. Only the semantic behavior is described; the code you’re seeing for removed tokens (105) is mentioned in other APIs, but there’s no spec line that says whether expired‑but‑existing tokens share that code or use a different one. So:
- 1) Answered – rolling 90 days from latest of initial link / renewal / last successful txn. - 2 & 3) Not specified in docs – please confirm timezone and the exact decline code with the Integration Team/product owner.
